what: Governs sale, discounting and assignment of receivables, including future receivables, with or without recourse.
impact: The legal basis for Factor's assignments; registration is what protects priority.

instrument: Federal Decree-Law 6 of 2025, Central Bank Law
what: Consolidates banking, finance companies, payments and insurance under CBUAE; fines up to ten times the violation.
impact: Sets the licence Factor needs and the penalty regime; the one-year reconciliation window has now closed.

what: Licensing and prudential rules for Finance Companies and Restricted Licence Finance Companies.
impact: The likely onshore licensing route; confirm with counsel whether discounting needs a full or restricted licence.

instrument: Health Insurance Claims Management Policy Directive
what: Replaces earlier Dubai claims rules: pre-authorisation, submission, adjudication, settlement and reconciliation timelines.
impact: Defines how and when claims Factor buys get paid; tracks the data Factor can verify against.

what: Insurers pay within 45 days of submission; a 0.03% daily fee applies to late payment.
impact: Anchors Factor's tenor and pricing; check whether the late fee follows the assigned claim.

instrument: Operational Risk and Operational Resilience Regulation (C1/2026)
what: Licensed institutions need frameworks for operational risk and resilience.
impact: Applies once licensed; Factor's AI-run screening and onboarding will need documented controls.

what: Tightens rules on marketing financial products and services.
impact: Shapes how Factor can run outbound sales to clinics.
